firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to ensure Authorization Independence, DBAC, and QAPs. User data is stored under `/users/{userId}` to establish clear ownership. Consultation logs are stored as subcollections under each user (`/users/{userId}/consultationLogs/{logId}`) to maintain the 1:N relationship and enforce ownership. This structure avoids `get()` calls in security rules because access control is based on path ownership (`request.auth.uid == userId`). Doctor data is stored in a separate collection `/doctors/{doctorId}`.  This design enables secure `list` operations for consultation logs (QAPs) because each user can only access their own logs. The denormalization strategy copies user ID into consultation logs, removing the need to fetch parent user data. The use of path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/...`) naturally supports private data access. No custom claims are needed because authorization relies on `request.auth.uid` and path ownership.
